strategic_horizon.terminal_goal: Ship a personal weak-network VPN with a portable Windows 11 x64 client and self-contained Linux amd64/arm64 server bundles. The public network must see exactly one long-lived TCP-shaped 4-tuple per VPN session: FakeTCP owns the flow from the initial SYN; the first few seconds carry a Reality-like/TLS-1.3-like bootstrap over that same flow; after bootstrap the same flow switches without FIN or a new SYN into WBD datagram transport carrying pinned wolfSSL DTLS 1.3 -> immutable LINK, with sustained payload never inheriting kernel TCP head-of-line blocking.
strategic_horizon.current_milestone: Architectural correction. The previous design used a kernel TCP Reality-like admission connection, closed it, then created a second independent raw FakeTCP connection. Physical and namespace/NAT testing exposed shared-port/conntrack instability and, more importantly, the user clarified that two public connections violate the original hard requirement. Stop repairing the dual-flow architecture. Replace it with one FakeTCP-owned public flow whose initial reliable phase is Reality-like enough to be externally indistinguishable at approximately 99% packet/handshake shape, then switch in-place to no-HOL DTLS/FEC/LINK payload semantics.
strategic_horizon.local_optimization_stop_rule: Do not preserve an old ADR or constitution clause merely because it freezes the dual-flow design. The user's newer hard constraint supersedes contradictory setup-only-separate-TCP wording. Preserve the validated release operating point (40 Mbit/s aggregate-inner on <=100 Mbit/s weak links), legacy FakeTCP recovery unless new single-flow work proves a required change, pinned wolfSSL DTLS 1.3, immutable LINK, one raw lane, and FEC off or fixed 20:20. The new architecture must use exactly one public TCP-shaped flow and must not route sustained payload through kernel TCP.

architecture_override.required_public_flow: Exactly one TCP-shaped 4-tuple for the entire VPN session. One SYN/SYNACK/ACK sequence only. No separate Reality TCP connection followed by FakeTCP. No second SYN after admission.
architecture_override.bootstrap_phase: FakeTCP owns the connection from SYN. During the first seconds it must provide a short reliable ordered bootstrap stream sufficient to emit and receive a normal-looking Reality-like/TLS-1.3-like handshake and admission exchange. If 100% byte/implementation identity with REALITY is impractical, target approximately 99% externally observable likeness without reintroducing kernel TCP ownership.
architecture_override.mode_switch: After authenticated bootstrap, remain on the same 4-tuple and same FakeTCP incarnation; transition in-band to datagram mode for pinned wolfSSL DTLS 1.3 and LINK. No FIN, no close/reconnect, no new SYN, and no kernel TCP takeover.
architecture_override.hol_rule: Kernel TCP may not carry sustained VPN payload. Any ordered/retransmitted behavior used for the bootstrap phase must be bounded to setup only. Post-switch loss recovery remains WBD/FakeTCP/DTLS/FEC controlled so one lost outer segment cannot impose normal TCP stream HOL on later VPN datagrams.
architecture_override.server_port_model: The final design must not depend on a kernel TCP Reality listener and a raw FakeTCP listener racing on the same public port for the same WBD session. FakeTCP is the WBD public-flow owner. Non-WBD fallback/cover behavior may require a classifier/front-end design, but it must not create a second WBD connection or corrupt the one WBD flow's sequence space.

continuation_cursor.why_now: The current code demonstrably creates two unrelated public connections: Windows Controller runs wbd-reality-front synchronously to obtain a ticket and only after it exits starts wbd-faketcp; server Reality front closes its TLS connection after ticket issuance. Physical tests and a NAT/shared-port sandbox exposed connection-state races, but the decisive issue is semantic: the user requires one public connection for the full session. Continuing to patch dual-flow conntrack behavior would optimize an architecture that violates the product requirement.
continuation_cursor.done_when: Architecture docs and code agree on one public flow. A deterministic namespace/NAT test proves exactly one SYN from WBD client through session teardown; the first phase parses as TLS-1.3/Reality-like setup and authenticates; an in-band mode switch occurs without FIN/new SYN; sustained DTLS/LINK traffic then survives loss/reordering without kernel-TCP HOL. Windows and Linux builds pass, single-flow reconnect/fault tests pass, 40 Mbit/s release-point gates pass, and only after those sandbox gates are green is a new Windows x64 + Linux ARM64 pair offered for physical qualification.
continuation_cursor.next_atomic_action: After refreshing live HEAD and this handoff, create a new single-flow architecture branch from the current canonical substantive checkpoint, not from PR #8's accumulated dual-flow experiments. First commit documentation/tests that make the hard invariant executable: one WBD public 4-tuple, one SYN only, FakeTCP owns sequence space from SYN, Reality-like TLS bootstrap is carried over a bounded reliable FakeTCP setup stream, explicit in-band setup->datagram switch, and no sustained kernel-TCP payload. Then implement the smallest vertical slice: FakeTCP reliable bootstrap byte-stream adapter plus TLS/Reality-like client/server over that adapter on Linux namespace loopback/NAT, followed by same-association DTLS handoff. Do not build Windows packages until the one-SYN Linux/NAT integration test is green.

local_test_snapshot.scope: Historical PR #8 dual-flow experiment only. Its sandbox work proved many lower layers but does not qualify the new one-public-flow requirement. The shared-port/NAT/reconnect work reproduced instability in the old architecture; do not treat this commit as a candidate release for the new architecture.

physical_e2e: A physical Windows 11 -> Ubuntu ARM64 run reached Reality AUTH OK, FakeTCP READY, DTLS server PEEK/HRR/ACCEPT PASS, READY role=server, and WBD_LINK_MUX_SESSION_READY once, proving the underlying FakeTCP->DTLS->LINK components can interoperate on real hosts.

Subsequent rapid physical attempts often showed Windows FakeTCP READY and DTLS CONNECT_START while the server did not spawn/reach the per-session DTLS worker, demonstrating instability before DTLS rather than a permanent wolfSSL incompatibility.
Readiness-gated Windows startup was valuable and should be preserved conceptually: do not mutate IPv6/routes or claim connect success before transport and LINK readiness.
dtls_and_certificate_sandbox: A Linux namespace integration test generated a temporary CA and SAN=wbd.test server certificate, compiled the pinned wolfSSL shim, and passed two simultaneous FakeTCP-mux inherited-worker DTLS 1.3 sessions with CA/hostname verification and bidirectional UDP echo.

DTLS stage markers observed server PEEK -> PEER_SET -> HRR_ARMED -> ACCEPT_START -> ACCEPT_PASS and client CONNECT_PASS. Therefore Linux inherited UDP worker, pinned wolfSSL DTLS 1.3, certificate verification, and bidirectional payload are not the architectural blocker.
rst_nat_sandbox: A NAT namespace A/B proved Linux clients generate kernel RSTs for raw FakeTCP-shaped flows. Allowing those RSTs through the router versus suppressing them did not prevent FakeTCP+DTLS from completing in that harness, so a blanket Windows RST firewall was not justified as a root-cause fix.

Windows Npcap mode handling had a real bug: pcap_setmode(handle, 0) was incorrectly documented as clearing SendToRx. Npcap 1.88 uses MODE_SENDTORX_CLEAR=0x0200. PR #8 corrected this and added a readiness marker. This fix may be retained when the Windows single-flow transport is rebuilt.
dual_flow_shared_port_reproduction: A stricter namespace/NAT harness added a real kernel TCP:443 listener alongside raw FakeTCP:443, matching the old server topology. It reproduced the physical failure shape: FakeTCP client READY, DTLS client CONNECT_START, but server mux never reached BOUND/DTLS worker creation.

This made shared kernel-TCP/raw-TCP sequence/conntrack competition a reproducible property of the old topology. Experimental same-4-tuple reincarnation and SYNACK-isolation work exists on PR #8, but the new product direction makes those mitigations historical diagnostics rather than the final architecture.
release_candidate_history: Before the architectural pivot, experimental D fixed FakeTCP mux worker timing, half-open cleanup and Linux raw EINTR handling and passed repeated mux-load RTT100 qualification. Those transport robustness lessons remain useful, but D still assumed separate Reality and FakeTCP public flows.

A later diagnostic build at source 6d96271bb4ad6f38caeececb7f83db9dd246160b passed main CI, Windows portable, Linux release, certificate mux, FakeTCP native and mux-load gates and produced verified Windows/Linux artifacts. Those artifacts are obsolete for the new single-flow architecture and must not be presented as final products.

implementation_direction.phase_0_tcp_shape: FakeTCP raw engine performs the only SYN/SYNACK/ACK on the public flow and owns all subsequent TCP header sequence/ack fields.
implementation_direction.phase_1_reliable_setup: Expose a bounded reliable ordered byte-stream abstraction over FakeTCP solely for setup. Feed that adapter to the Reality-like/TLS client and server so the observable early exchange is normal TLS 1.3 / Reality-like rather than a separate kernel TCP connection. This phase may retransmit and order bytes because it is short setup traffic; its HOL behavior must terminate at the mode switch.
implementation_direction.phase_2_switch: Authenticate and derive/confirm session identity inside the setup stream, then exchange an authenticated mode-switch record that both endpoints acknowledge. Do not close the outer flow. Reset/advance only WBD internal delivery state as formally specified; public 4-tuple and FakeTCP incarnation remain unchanged.
implementation_direction.phase_3_datagram: After switch, feed datagrams on the same FakeTCP association to pinned wolfSSL DTLS 1.3, then immutable LINK/FEC. Data segments must not wait for earlier lost datagrams except where WBD recovery/FEC explicitly requires it; normal TCP cumulative-stream HOL is forbidden.
implementation_direction.cover_and_fallback_question: Non-WBD clients hitting the public port still need plausible fallback/cover behavior. Solve this as a classifier/response problem around the FakeTCP-owned public ingress, not by making the WBD client first create a separate kernel TCP admission connection. This is a design item for the new ADR and tests.

product_policy.linux_server: One public WBD_PORT. Final single-flow design must have one WBD raw FakeTCP owner for WBD sessions from SYN through teardown; loopback LINK/platform remain internal. Firewall cleanup remains WBD-owned only.
product_policy.windows: Portable x64 wbd.exe, UAC elevation, Npcap 1.88, Full/Foreign/China routes, Auto/System/Cloudflare/Custom DNS, device-wide IPv6 kill-switch while connected. Preserve dependency readiness gating, but replace separate Reality-bootstrap process plus later FakeTCP connect with one FakeTCP-owned flow containing setup and datagram phases.
product_policy.transport: One public TCP-shaped flow; Reality-like/TLS-like bootstrap first; in-place no-new-SYN transition to pinned wolfSSL DTLS 1.3 -> immutable LINK; one raw lane; FEC off or fixed 20:20; release point remains 40 Mbit/s aggregate-inner on <=100 Mbit/s weak links until requalified.
